title: Unbounded support calculus from exact abelian open/closed localization data
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_X,\mathcal A_U,\mathcal A_Z$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose additive exact functors $J:\mathcal A_U\to\mathcal A_X$, $P:\mathcal A_X\to\mathcal A_U$, $Q:\mathcal A_X\to\mathcal A_Z$, $I:\mathcal A_Z\to\mathcal A_X$ have specified adjunctions $J\dashv P$ and $Q\dashv I$. Assume the open unit $1\to PJ$ and closed counit $QI\to1$ are invertible, $PI=0$, $QJ=0$, and the actual counit and unit form a short exact sequence
$$0\to JP M\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow IQ M\to0$$
for every $M\in\mathcal A_X$. Exact means preserving finite limits and finite colimits; short exact has its abelian-category meaning.

Then termwise application descends to functors on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. The localized units and counits give adjunctions $D(J)\dashv D(P)$ and $D(Q)\dashv D(I)$, with their actual triangle identities. The open unit and closed counit remain invertible and the two mixed restrictions remain zero. The pair $(D(P),D(Q))$ jointly reflects isomorphisms. For any $H\in D(\mathcal A_X)$ with $D(P)H=0$, the closed unit $H\to D(I)D(Q)H$ is invertible. Restriction $D(Q)$ is fully faithful on the essential image of $D(I)$. No boundedness, enough-injectives or recollement theorem is assumed.

proof.text: For each $F\in\{J,P,Q,I\}$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. All four functors are additive and preserve finite limits and finite colimits by hypothesis, so termwise $C(F)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and factors as $D(F)$ on the ordinary unbounded derived category. Write $q_T:C(\mathcal A_T)\to D(\mathcal A_T)$ for localization and $a_{F,K}:D(F)(q_SK)\xrightarrow{\sim}q_TC(F)K$ for the factorization isomorphisms. Every derived object is represented by a complex as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; no resolution or bound is introduced.

Use the specified exact-derived adjunction construction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] for $J\dashv P$ and $Q\dashv I$. Here is the normalization explicitly. For an exact pair $F\dashv G$ with unit $u$ and counit $v$, transposition degree by degree gives the cochain adjunction: the differential equation for a transposed map follows from naturality of $u,v$, and the inverse equations hold in each degree. The derived unit at $q_SK$ is the composite
$$q_SK\xrightarrow{q_S(C(u)_K)}q_SC(G)C(F)K\xrightarrow{a_{G,C(F)K}^{-1}}D(G)q_TC(F)K\xrightarrow{D(G)(a_{F,K}^{-1})}D(G)D(F)q_SK.$$
The derived counit at $q_TL$ is
$$D(F)D(G)q_TL\xrightarrow{D(F)(a_{G,L})}D(F)q_SC(G)L\xrightarrow{a_{F,C(G)L}}q_TC(F)C(G)L\xrightarrow{q_T(C(v)_L)}q_TL.$$
These extend uniquely to natural transformations by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2), with the exact termwise factorizations of step 1. Thus the maps are the localizations of the given maps, rather than newly chosen adjunction maps.

proof.text: Check the two triangle identities for the maps in step 2 after precomposition with $q_S$ or $q_T$. Under the $a_F,a_G$ identifications, the two composites become respectively $q_T(C(v)_{C(F)K}\circ C(F)(C(u)_K))$ and $q_S(C(G)(C(v)_L)\circ C(u)_{C(G)L})$. In each degree these are $v_{F(K^n)}\circ F(u_{K^n})=1$ and $G(v_{L^n})\circ u_{G(L^n)}=1$, the original triangle identities. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] implies equality with the identity transformations on the derived categories. Hence the actual localized maps satisfy both triangles for both adjunctions.

proof.text: The open unit $1\to PJ$ and closed counit $QI\to1$ are isomorphisms on each object by assumption, so their termwise maps have inverse chain maps (the component inverses are natural). Their localized maps in step 2 are therefore isomorphisms. More formally, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) lifts these transformations and their inverses and preserves both inverse equations. Likewise the specified zero functor identities $PI=0$ and $QJ=0$ give termwise natural isomorphisms $C(P)C(I)\cong0$ and $C(Q)C(J)\cong0$. The factorizations from step 1 make $D(P)D(I)$ and $D(Q)D(J)$ lifts of their localizations; clause (2) identifies them with the zero functors. Zero objects remain zero here because the localizations in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] are additive and their zero complex represents zero. These arguments also show that the four induced functors preserve zero objects.

proof.text:
For every integer $n$ and every $F\in\{J,P,Q,I\}$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] supplies a natural isomorphism $H^n(C(F)K)\cong F(H^n(K))$ on all cochain complexes. Combine it with $a_F$ and with $H^nq\cong H^n$ from [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both sides invert quasi-isomorphisms, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) therefore lifts this isomorphism to
$$c_F^n:H^nD(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}F H^n.$$
This is natural for every derived morphism, since it is a lifted natural transformation, not merely an objectwise identification. It is only the existing cochain cohomology comparison descended through localization.

proof.text:
Let $b:K\to L$ be any derived morphism such that $D(P)b$ and $D(Q)b$ are invertible. Step 5 and naturality give that $P(H^n b)$ and $Q(H^n b)$ are invertible for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. Apply the assumed abelian localization sequence to the two objects $H^nK,H^nL$. Naturality of the actual open counit $JP\to1$ and closed unit $1\to IQ$ gives a commutative diagram of short exact rows with vertical maps
$$JP(H^n b),\quad H^n b,\quad IQ(H^n b).$$
The outside maps are invertible since functors preserve inverses. By [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma] the middle map is invertible. This holds for every integer $n$, so [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] gives that $b$ is invertible. This proves joint reflection without assuming either restriction is individually conservative and without applying a bounded-below criterion.

proof.text: Abbreviate $\bar P=D(P),\bar Q=D(Q),\bar I=D(I)$ and let $\eta:1\to\bar I\bar Q$, $\epsilon:\bar Q\bar I\to1$ be the closed maps already constructed. Suppose $\bar PH=0$. Then $\bar P(\eta_H)$ is a map between zero objects, since $\bar P\bar I=0$ by step 4, and is thus invertible. The left triangle identity of step 3 reads $\epsilon_{\bar QH}\circ\bar Q(\eta_H)=1_{\bar QH}$. Since $\epsilon$ is invertible by step 4, $\bar Q(\eta_H)=\epsilon_{\bar QH}^{-1}$ is invertible. Joint reflection from step 6 applied to the specific morphism $\eta_H$ proves that the actual support unit $H\to\bar I\bar QH$ is invertible.

source.place: (2), exact open/closed adjunction route; elementary consequence of the preceding joint reflection and the closed triangle identity

proof.text:
If $X,Y$ lie in the essential image of $\bar I$, then $\bar PX=\bar PY=0$ by step 4, so $\eta_X,\eta_Y$ are invertible by step 7. For every $a:\bar QX\to\bar QY$ define
$$s(a)=\eta_Y^{-1}\circ\bar I(a)\circ\eta_X:X\to Y.$$
For $b:X\to Y$, naturality $\bar I\bar Q(b)\circ\eta_X=\eta_Y\circ b$ gives $s(\bar Qb)=b$. Conversely $\bar Q\eta_T=\epsilon_{\bar QT}^{-1}$ from step 7 and naturality $\epsilon_{\bar QY}\circ\bar Q\bar I(a)=a\circ\epsilon_{\bar QX}$ give
$$\bar Qs(a)=\epsilon_{\bar QY}\circ\bar Q\bar I(a)\circ\epsilon_{\bar QX}^{-1}=a.$$
Thus $s$ is an explicit inverse to the map on Hom sets induced by $\bar Q$, which proves full faithfulness of restriction on the full essential-image subcategory. All arguments used arbitrary integer degrees or adjunction equations; none used injective resolutions, boundedness, or a recollement theorem.
